floor_history.headline: Recon: rule-era chassis discarded; fresh indexed pure-C derivation reaches 34 honest / 28 with a diagnostic biv-elimination blocker; dominant residual mechanism identified as loop.c biv elimination of

F1 and F2 both SOLVED: loop.c biv elimination blocked honestly via per-iteration record pointers (all_reduced=0 path) and the li-1 hoist blocked via two non-consecutive sets; floor 34 -> 20 with build

frontier.hypothesis: An honest (non-variable-reuse) spelling gives the 1-holding pseudo two non-consecutive sets, removing the only family-gated construct from the candidate.
frontier.mechanism: scan_loop movable creation requires n_times_set==1 or consecutive sets (loop.c:705-708). A real flag local written 1 in the if-arm and 0 in the else-arm, stored inside each arm, gives n_times_set==2 with non-adjacent sets; combine should fold the 0 arm to 'sh zero,4(a2)' since the MIPS movhi pattern accepts const_int 0 via $zero, while the 1 arm keeps its li.
frontier.next_probe: Apply that flag-local variant on top of memory/grind/func_80019568/candidate.c and measure; target is 20 with build_insns 141. If it holds, the whole loop-1 form is ordinary C with no family claim.

frontier.hypothesis: R1's v0<->v1 swap is a local-alloc seat assignment, reachable by a C lever the solver can name.
frontier.mechanism: Target ties 'voice' to the lbu temp's seat (srl v0,v0,4) and puts the lhu temp in v1; ours is the mirror. Declaration-order swaps (voice before/after voice2) measured INERT, so spelling guesses are exhausted at the cheap end.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/ra_solver (inverse.py / inverse_compose.py classify) against tmp/grind/func_80019568/dumps/code6cac.lreg for the loop-1 block and get a REACHABLE/FORECLOSED verdict plus a ranked C-lever vector before spending more measurements.

frontier.hypothesis: An honest producer exists for the tail's register-held &D_80102790 across the load and the store.
frontier.mechanism: Aggregate (H8) and statement-order (H9) explanations are both KILLED. What remains is why cse/combine did not share one address register between the two (mem (symbol_ref D_80102790)) accesses, and whether an ordinary-C read-modify-write spelling forces it.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_80019568/dumps/code6cac.cse and .combine for the tail block; then grep docs/reference/sotn-construct-index.md for a load+store-through-one-address-register global RMW precedent; then read .claude/rules/pointer-rmw-global-sanctioned.md BEFORE assuming .claude/rules/pointer-alias-fake-exception.md applies.

judge_constraints: LAYER-1 CHEAT-REVIEWER FAIL: C1 (record pointers) and C3 (pointer RMW on D_80102790) pass; C2 (the two-armed `s32 enable;` flag local) is a novel shape that does not fit inside named-local-fake-exception's exact sanctioned scope and has no other precedent covering it. Next action: Do not commit. C1 (rec/o record pointers) and C3 (s32 *p RMW on D_80102790, which matches pointer-rmw-global-sanctioned.md's exact worked shape and has documented lever-exhaustion via H8/H9/H11) are clean and unaffected. C2 alone blocks the commit: file a family-candidate entry in docs/grind/borderline.md describing

The ban is narrowed to the UNINITIALISED dead-assignment shape (`s32 enable;` with `enable = 0; o[2] = enable;` in the else arm); the default-initialised flag whose initialiser is read on the else path is permitted, must keep the /* FAKE */ annotation, and must be filed under duplicated-statement-into-arms (not named-local-fake-exception).
